newsitem.title: USA: PG&E projects average year for hydropower.
newsitem.headline: PG&E projects average year for hydropower.

text.p: PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas and Electric Co projects average hydropower output this year based on March snowpack figures, a company spokesman said.
PG&E averages around 12,500 gigawatt hours (GWh) per year in hydropower generation, but actual output ranges widely.
Early March measurements showed California statewide snowpack at 115 percent of average levels, down from from estimates earlier this winter.
The PG&E spokesman cautioned there is still time for winter precipitation to move higher or lower, with early April generally marking the peak for California snowpack volumes.
In addition, "market conditions will dictate the degree to which you use hydro resources," spokesman Bill Sessa said.
"For instance, BPA (Bonneville Power Administration) is shopping lots of hydropower," he added.
Last year, hydropower accounted for 17.2 percent of PG&E's total power generation, or about 14,000 GWh.
This year it is expected to provide between 16 and 19 percent of total generation, Sessa said.

In 1995, California's wettest year since the early 1980s, hydropower provided more than 20 percent of PG&E's total generation portfolio, while 1994 hydropower output accounted for just over 7 percent of total power generation.

California's other major investor owned utility, Southern California Edison Co, said last week it expected hydropower resources to provide 5,600 GWh of its 1997 power generation, compared with a long-term average near 4,800 GWh.
